observation.visible_scene: An open, rocky landscape (quarry- or spoil-heap-like) under a partly cloudy sky. The foreground holds a static pile of pale broken rocks and bare dirt with tire tracks; behind it rises a long dark mound of rubble. From the crest of that mound a blast is already erupting, throwing up a column of dark debris and white smoke. The camera position and framing do not change across the segment (foreground pile and ridge line stay fixed), so all motion belongs to the erupting material, not to the camera.
visible_changes: At t=0 the eruption is already underway: a compact dark plume topped by white smoke rises from the mound crest; no onset or trigger is shown.
The dark debris column grows taller and broader, transitioning from a tight plume into a wide fan-shaped spray of individual dark particles scattered high against the sky.
White smoke billows at the base and mid-section of the plume and, over time, spreads laterally, rolling outward to the right along the ground surface.
The airborne dark-particle cloud continuously expands upward and outward, reaching near the top of the frame by the end while still dispersing.

The foreground rock pile, the dirt ground, and the dark ridge behind the mound remain in the same image positions throughout, confirming a static viewpoint and that the visible motion is the blast ejecta and smoke, not scene translation.
The eruption is still actively expanding at the final frame; it does not settle or complete within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or trigger of the blast (detonation, collapse, etc.) and the exact moment of initiation, which precede this cropped segment.
The later outcome: how the debris and smoke eventually settle and the final shape of the mound.
Whether the dark mound itself shifts or slumps beneath the ejecta, which is largely hidden by the smoke.
uncertain_details: The identity of the flying dark particles (rock, soil, or other debris) and of the white plume (steam, dust, or combustion smoke) cannot be confirmed from the images.
Whether the rightward-rolling white cloud is ground-hugging smoke or dust kicked up along the surface is not distinguishable.
The precise height and spread of the ejecta beyond the frame edges are unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
